publications.summary: A qualitative study of how translation students interpret the cultural positions and viewpoints in an online British news text.
publications.method: Thirteen students completed a reading and translation task. Five also took part in interviews and screen recordings of their online activity.
findings: Many participants had difficulty identifying the viewpoint expressed in the text.
The analysis linked these difficulties to limited attention to sociocultural context and ineffective use of online reading resources.
publications.use: Use this study to inform research on critical digital reading and to design activities that ask learners to examine a text’s author, audience, cultural references and viewpoint.
publications.scope: A small qualitative study of one reading task; its contribution concerns reading practices and interpretation.
publications.title: Desenredando la web: la lectura crítica de los aprendices de lenguas extranjeras en entornos digitales
publications.alternate_title: Untangling the web: critical reading of foreign languages students in digital environments

publications.summary: An investigation of how secondary-school learners use machine translation for reading and writing, and how teachers respond to these practices.
publications.method: A qualitative, multilingual case study in two Catalan schools, using interviews, classroom observation and recordings of screen activity.
findings: The study describes different levels of teacher permission and student uses for comprehension, composition and revision.
Learners’ checking strategies vary in sophistication, pointing to a need for critical guidance in using language technologies.
publications.use: Use the paper when examining machine translation literacy or planning classroom discussion of verification, revision and preparation of input texts.
publications.scope: The study concerns the machine translation tools and school practices observed at the time of the research.
publications.title: Aprender lengua con el traductor automático en la escuela secundaria: un diálogo necesario
publications.alternate_title: Machine translation as a tool for foreign language learning in secondary schools: A necessary dialogue

publications.short_title: The literacy ecology of a gamer
publications.summary: A case study of the literacy practices and language learning involved in translating video games and participating in online gaming communities.
publications.method: Digital ethnography combining interviews, online observation and screen recordings of a gamer’s translation workflow.
findings: Game translation involves linguistic, technical and sociocultural literacies across a network of online spaces.
Community feedback creates situated opportunities to discuss language and revise translations.
publications.use: Use this study in work on gaming literacies, affinity spaces and informal language learning, or as an example of studying the activity surrounding a digital text.
publications.scope: An exploratory single-participant case study, interpreted through New Literacy Studies.

publications.short_title: Fan translation across games, anime and fanfiction
publications.summary: A comparison of three fan translators working with games, anime subtitles and fanfiction, connecting their translation activity with language learning.
publications.method: Qualitative digital ethnography using interviews, screenshots and screen recordings, framed by New Literacy Studies.
findings: Translation provides opportunities for agency, creativity and identity work in fan communities.
The cases show language learning through peer feedback, independent inquiry and resourceful use of translation tools.
publications.use: Use the study to examine fan translation as a social literacy practice and to inform activities connecting learner interests, translation and collaborative feedback.
publications.scope: Three qualitative cases across different fandoms and language combinations.

publications.short_title: Guerrilla fan translation and language reflection
publications.summary: A study of a Catalan-speaking gaming community translating games from English into Catalan, with attention to collaboration and discussion about language.
publications.method: Digital ethnography with online interviews and observation; content analysis and focused analysis of metalinguistic discussions.
findings: The translators develop shared roles and a community identity connected with producing cultural content in Catalan.
Language learning opportunities arise through translating, discussing doubts with peers and reviewing prospective members’ translation tests.
publications.use: Use this study for research on collaborative translation, language learning in digital wilds and the role of metalinguistic discussion in translation-based teaching.
publications.scope: Qualitative evidence from one fan-translation community.

publications.short_title: Informal digital learning of English: a scoping review
publications.summary: A review mapping research on informal digital learning of English and identifying questions for language education and future investigation.
publications.method: A Web of Science search of research published between 1980 and 2019. Thirty studies met the review’s inclusion criteria.
findings: The literature covers linguistic, affective and cultural dimensions, alongside agency and digital literacies.
Mixed methods and qualitative approaches predominate; only two included studies used longitudinal data collection.
publications.use: Use this review to frame an IDLE study, identify methodological gaps and situate work on language learning beyond the classroom.
publications.scope: The review reflects its database, search terms, inclusion criteria and historical search window.

publications.short_title: Learning Spanish through vlogging on Bilibili
publications.summary: A study of Chinese learners’ Spanish-language vlogs on Bilibili, examining video production, multilingual writing and interaction around learning.
publications.method: Qualitative virtual ethnography and analysis of 134 Chinese-produced Spanish-language vlogs.
findings: Vloggers combine resources from formal education and informal media practices.
Subtitles, translation, feedback requests and danmu comments support multimodal expression and reflection on language.
publications.use: Use this study to inform research on learner-created video and to consider multilingual subtitles, reflection and peer feedback in language-learning projects.
publications.scope: The findings describe practices on one platform and in a particular learner context.

publications.short_title: Serious games, vocabulary and healthcare knowledge
publications.summary: A mixed-methods study of whether a serious game can support healthcare content learning and incidental English vocabulary acquisition.
publications.method: Iranian nursing students learned through Saving Lives or traditional instruction, with 80 participants in each group. Evidence included pre/post tests and questionnaire responses.
findings: The game group showed significantly greater improvements in healthcare knowledge and incidental vocabulary acquisition.
The study discusses engagement, multimodal contextual information and repeated encounters with vocabulary in gameplay.
publications.use: Use this study when investigating content and language learning through games, designing English for specific purposes activities, or comparing game-based and conventional instruction.
publications.scope: Evidence from a specific game, nursing-education context and study design; transfer to other settings requires evaluation.

publications.short_title: Learning Korean through TikTok and YouTube comments
publications.summary: An analysis of comments on Korean-learning videos, examining what participation around social media content contributes to language learning.
publications.method: Exploratory observation of TikTok and YouTube and analysis of 570 English- and Spanish-language comments.
findings: Comments address creators, the community and questions about Korean, supporting resource sharing and language reflection.
The analysed comments contain no interaction in Korean: engagement around a language does not necessarily provide practice in that language.
publications.use: Use the study to examine comment-based learning or to design activities that connect language reflection with opportunities for target-language interaction.
publications.scope: Findings concern the sampled comments and videos, rather than measured changes in proficiency.
publications.access_note: A public repository copy is available on Zenodo.

publications.summary: A study of how preservice language teachers use memes to narrate experiences and express identities as learners and future teachers.
publications.method: Discourse and thematic analysis of 777 memes in stories created by 84 preservice teachers from pedagogy and linguistics cohorts.
findings: The cohorts express different emphases in learning experiences, teaching aspirations and anxieties.
Humour and translingual choices reveal aspects of identity that can inform reflective work in teacher education.
publications.use: Use this paper to inform research on teacher identity or to consider Story by Memes as a reflective narrative activity alongside existing teacher-education practices.
publications.scope: The findings are grounded in two cohorts; adapting the activity requires attention to participants and context.

publications.summary: A study of how game translation and written community interaction bring language attitudes and Catalan identity into view.
publications.method: Analysis of online multiparty written interaction among 15 Catalan-speaking gamers translating games from English into Catalan.
findings: Translation routines and membership tests give rise to discussion of language norms, Spanish–Catalan interference and creative language choices.
These discussions connect translation decisions with grassroots linguistic activism and identity development.
publications.use: Use the study in research on minoritized languages, language ideology and fan communities, or when examining how translation decisions express cultural and linguistic positions.
publications.scope: A situated qualitative analysis of one community and language pair.
publications.access_note: The University of Groningen provides a repository version under its Taverne access terms.

publications.short_title: From Foe to Friend: fan translation in education
publications.summary: A pedagogical chapter exploring how fan translation can become a communicative and creative language-learning activity.
publications.method: A conceptual and practice-oriented chapter presenting five proposals for incorporating fan translation into language education.
findings: The proposals connect translation with learner interests, audiences and collaborative problem-solving.
Bridging activities provide a way to relate informal fan practices to classroom language work.
publications.use: Use the chapter when planning translation projects, discussing the educational role of fan cultures or designing tasks around cultural and linguistic mediation.
publications.scope: Pedagogical proposals to adapt and evaluate in context.
publications.journal: Translation, Translanguaging and Machine Translation in Foreign Language Education
publications.book: Translation, Translanguaging and Machine Translation in Foreign Language Education

publications.short_title: Digital literacies in Spanish language education
publications.summary: A conceptual chapter on digital literacies for Spanish as a second language, bringing sociocultural, multilingual and multimodal perspectives into language education.
publications.method: A review of concepts, epistemological and methodological approaches, with illustrative studies and didactic suggestions.
findings: Digital literacy is approached as a dynamic, situated set of discourse practices.
Connections between practices inside and outside classrooms inform ways of approaching digitally mediated communication in L2 education.
publications.use: Use this chapter to frame research on digital literacies or to develop teaching that attends to audience, context, multilingual resources and multimodal meaning.
publications.scope: A conceptual and pedagogical chapter, with examples to consider in relation to local teaching contexts.
publications.journal: The Routledge Handbook of Multiliteracies for Spanish Language Teaching
publications.book: The Routledge Handbook of Multiliteracies for Spanish Language Teaching: multimodalidad e interdisciplinariedad

publications.short_title: Fan and ludic practices for EFL writing and reflection
publications.summary: A practical chapter introducing Story by Memes as a multimodal writing and reflection activity for advanced language learners and student teachers.
publications.method: A practice-oriented activity sequence informed by fan cultures, play and bridging activities.
findings: Meme composition makes learners’ interests, language experiences and prospective teacher identities available for discussion.
The sequence creates opportunities for discourse choices and reflection on writing and digital literacies.
publications.use: Use the chapter to plan or adapt a meme-based narrative task, connecting composition, presentation and reflective discussion with a course’s language and teacher-education goals.
publications.scope: An adaptable pedagogical sequence; outcomes should be evaluated in the setting where it is used.
publications.journal: New Language Learning and Teaching Environments
publications.book: Technology and English Language Teaching in a Changing World: A Practical Guide for Teachers and Teacher Educators

publications.short_title: Teenagers’ identities and language practices on YouTube
publications.summary: A study of how Catalan teenage gamers present themselves on YouTube through language, images and video-related literacy practices.
publications.method: Digital ethnography with three teenage gamers, drawing on interviews, screenshots and video analysis through New Literacy Studies.
findings: The cases show different degrees of participation and specialisation on YouTube.
Choices of usernames, images and language reveal varying linguistic and multimodal awareness across Catalan, Spanish and English.
publications.use: Use the chapter in research on youth digital identities and multilingual media practices, or to inform reflection on self-presentation and audience in student video projects.
publications.scope: Three situated qualitative cases of teenage gamers.
publications.journal: New Language Learning and Teaching Environments
publications.book: Technology and the Psychology of Second Language Learners and Users

publications.summary: A discourse-analytic study of how language teachers make sense of artificial intelligence through metaphors, evaluative positions and pedagogical expectations.
publications.method: Discourse analysis of language teachers’ attitudes towards artificial intelligence.
findings: The article foregrounds teachers’ interpretations of AI and their implications for language education.
publications.use: Use the paper when examining teacher discourse, pedagogical judgement and the role of AI in language teacher education.
publications.scope: Read the publisher’s article for the full analysis, evidence and methodological details.
publications.access_note: Full text is available through the publisher. The site links to the journal version while access and embargo conditions apply.
